title: Compression Through Time: An Interplay of Separability, Stationarity and Capacity
abstract: arXiv:2610.16660v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Information-theoretic and geometric compression have been widely studied as possible explanations for generalization. Yet their temporal dynamics in recurrent networks remain largely unexplored. Using discretized LSTMs, whose finite embedding space enables direct estimates of information quantities, we observe pronounced compression across the final timesteps of many datasets. We explain this effect through three competing mechanisms: (i) class separability permits stronger compression at the final timestep; (ii) shared recurrent dynamics propagate this pressure across timesteps with similar activation states, making its extent depend on temporal stationarity; and (iii) limited representational capacity opposes prolonged compression because it restricts information available for subsequent computation. translated_title: 随时间的压缩：可分性、平稳性与容量的相互作用
translated_abstract: 信息论压缩和几何压缩作为对泛化现象的可能解释已被广泛研究，然而它们在循环网络中的时间动态在很大程度上仍未被探索。我们使用离散化的LSTM——其有限的嵌入空间使得可以直接估计信息量——观察到在许多数据集的最后几个时间步上存在明显的压缩现象。我们通过三种相互竞争的机制来解释这一效应：(i) 类别可分性允许在最终时间步实现更强的压缩；(ii) 共享的循环动力学将这种压力传播到具有相似激活状态的时间步上，使压缩程度取决于时间平稳性；(iii) 有限的表示容量会对抗持续的压缩，因为它限制了可用于后续计算的信息量。我们通过受控的合成干预和真实世界的序列任务系统地测试了这些机制。我们的结果识别了（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了循环网络中的信息压缩现象由类别可分性、时间平稳性和有限的表示容量这三种相互竞争的机制共同驱动。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that information compression in recurrent networks over time is driven by the interplay of three competing mechanisms: class separability, temporal stationarity, and limited representational capacity.
